newsitem.title: USA: Bethlehem Steel to close Maryland plant.
newsitem.headline: Bethlehem Steel to close Maryland plant.

text.p: Bethlehem Steel Corp said on Wednesday it has notified workers of of a planned permanent shutdown of its BethShip Sparrows Point Yard.
Bethlehem said it was issuing this notice at this time because of the breakdown in negotiations between WHX Corp, which is negotiating to buy the Yard, and labor unions.
The company informed the 900 workers about the planned shutdown under the Worker Adjustment and Retraining Act.
A Bethlehem Steel spokesman said it has issued the notice to employees, which means that unprofitable shipbuilding and ship repair yard will close sometime after 60 days.
Federal law requires large companies to give workers advance notice for closings, a Bethlehem spokesman said. the plant has been unprofitable
Bethlehem said the ship yard will take no additional orders other than those which could be completed within the timeframe of its current order book, unless the yard can be sold.
Bethlehem announced in October 1996 that it planned to sell the yard as part of a comprehensive restructuring plan and said at that time that if the yard could not be sold it would be shut down.
A restructuring charge for this plan was recorded in the fourth quarter 1996, the company said.

WHX Corp, a prospective buyer, was in talks with the Industrial Union of Marine and Shipbuilding Workers of America and the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers, Bethlehem said.
